::: {.callout-note}
## About

Python (Jupyter) cells with `panzoom: true`, next to Quarto's
`lightbox: true`: panzoom takes every image the lightbox would, except
where a case asks for the lightbox.
[`j-jupyter-lightbox`](j-jupyter-lightbox.html) has the same cases without
panzoom: compare each case with the same number there. The knitr
equivalent is [`c-panzoom-auto`](c-panzoom-auto.html).

```yaml
filters:
  - panzoom
panzoom: true
lightbox: true
```

Jupyter leaves the `panzoom` and `lightbox` options out of the code shown
on the page; the **Code** button at the top shows the full source.
:::

The cases below share this setup:

```{python}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

x = np.linspace(0, 4 * np.pi, 400)
```

## 1. Figure with a caption {#c1 expect-open="panzoom"}

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "A sine wave."

plt.plot(x, np.sin(x))
plt.show()
```

## 2. Plot without a caption {#c2 expect-open="panzoom"}

```{python}
plt.plot(x, np.cos(x))
plt.show()
```

## 3. Subfigures (fig-subcap, layout-ncol) {#c3 expect-open="panzoom"}

```{python}
#| label: fig-pair
#| fig-cap: "Two waves."
#| fig-subcap: ["Sine", "Cosine"]
#| layout-ncol: 2

plt.plot(x, np.sin(2 * x))
plt.show()
plt.plot(x, np.cos(2 * x))
plt.show()
```

## 4. Nested `lightbox:` options {#c4 expect-open="glightbox"}

A cell's own `lightbox:` options ask for Quarto's lightbox, so panzoom
leaves the cell to it, as with knitr ([`c-panzoom-auto`](c-panzoom-auto.html), cases 6 and 7). With
Jupyter, Quarto's lightbox ignores the options themselves: the group and
description don't reach it.

```{python}
#| lightbox:
#|   group: waves
#|   description: "Ignored by Quarto's lightbox with Jupyter."

plt.plot(x, np.sin(3 * x))
plt.show()
plt.plot(x, np.cos(3 * x))
plt.show()
```

## 5. `lightbox: false` {#c5 expect-open="nothing"}

Opted out of the lightbox; panzoom leaves an explicit lightbox setting
alone too.

```{python}
#| lightbox: false

plt.plot(x, np.sin(4 * x))
plt.show()
```

## 6. `panzoom: true` on a cell {#c6 expect-open="panzoom"}

With the panzoom filter loaded, the option marks the plot for panzoom
ahead of the document's `lightbox: true`.

```{python}
#| panzoom: true

plt.plot(x, np.cos(4 * x))
plt.show()
```
